title: SDK Cheat-Packs: Lightweight Playflows v2 (draft)
content:
Purpose:
Short, snackable "cheat-packs" for engineers integrating Redwood SDKs. Focus: friction-free first 10 minutes, common failure modes, and minimal telemetry hooks that help us iterate fast.

Audience:
- Product engineers prototyping features
- Platform engineers embedding Redwood SDK into internal services
- Solutions engineers running customer sandboxes

High-level constraints / decisions (why this doc exists):
- Keep each flow to <= 6 discrete steps so a dev can read + try in ~10 minutes.
- Prefer local-first examples (no infra needed) and one canonical production snippet.
- Make failure modes explicit and trivial to reproduce locally so support can triage quickly.
- Include 3 telemetry metrics to unblock product/infra triage without overwhelming customers.

1) 10-minute "Hello, Redwood" flow (node/python examples)
- Goal: create an API key, run a single generation, stream result locally.
Steps:
  1) Create free dev API key in Console (or use sandbox key).
  2) Install SDK: npm i @redwood/sdk or pip install redwood-sdk.
  3) Run short script below.
  4) Observe streaming tokens in terminal and check Console traces.
  5) If no output, run: env REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=debug node hello.js to see network/handshake.
  6) Open Console > Requests > trace id (from SDK logs) to inspect routing and model selection.

Node minimal (paste into hello.js):
const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdk');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
(async () => {
  const stream = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-medium', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Write a haiku about shipping.' }] });
  for await (const chunk of stream) console.log(chunk.text);
})();

Python minimal (hello.py):
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
for chunk in client.chat.stream(model='redwood-medium', messages=[{'role':'user','content':'Write a haiku about shipping.'}]):
    print(chunk.text, end='')

2) Sandbox/no-key dev loop (fast feedback)
- Start local proxy stub (./scripts/dev-stub) to avoid using real tokens. The stub emulates response latency and simple errors.
- Use env var REDWOOD_LOCAL_STUB=true to switch SDK target.
- Add minimal fakes for streaming and error injection (details in /scripts).

3) Production integration checklist (minimal gating)
- Pin SDK version in package manager (no alpha channel).
- Set REDWOOD_API_KEY via secret manager (KMS/HSM recommended for regulated customers).
- Enable telemetry flags (see telemetry section).
- Configure model pinning: model: 'redwood-large:2026-01-12' (locks weights + perf profile).
- Canary: 1% traffic for 24h -> compare latency and token cost to baseline.

4) Common failure modes + quick triage steps
- Handshake failure (SDK logs: "auth failed"): check key scopes, time skew, and proxy. Repro: curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health with header Authorization: Bearer <key>.
- Streaming stalls after first token: check network MTU, middlebox buffering. Workaround: set STREAM_CHUNK_MS=50 to force regular flush.
- Silent high latency: check Console for routing fallback to cheaper region/model. If so, force region via client config: region: 'us-east-1'.
- Unexpected output quality regression: run prompt-based canary test (see tiny-evals snippet below) and open issue JIRA-DEVEXP-789 with trace ids and prompt set.

5) Tiny-evals quick harness (local)
- Purpose: smoke-test quality after SDK/model changes.
- Inputs: 8 canonical prompts (stored in /examples/tiny-evals/prompts.json).
- Compare: token accuracy (basic string match heuristics) + perplexity proxy by response length.
- If delta > 12% on pass rate, block rollout and file regression (tag: regress-quality).

6) Telemetry (minimum useful set)
- Metrics (names we onboard into Console and SRE dashboards):
  - sdk.init_time_ms (histogram) — time to initialize client (useful for cold-starts).
  - sdk.request_first_token_ms (p50/p95) — latency to first token for streaming requests.
  - sdk.request_tokens_consumed (counter by model) — token consumption per route.
- Logs: include request_id, model, client_version, route, truncated prompt (50 chars) — avoid PII.
- Traces: link request spans to Console trace id. Ensure SDK attaches trace id header: x-redwood-trace-id.

7) Release & rollout heuristics (recommended)
- Patch: automatic 100% after smoke + integration tests pass.
- Minor (features): canary 5% for 48h, monitor sdk.init_time_ms and request_first_token_ms.
- Major (model changes / behavioral changes): canary 1% for 72h + manual review with product.

8) Example tiny README for new integrator (copyable)
Title: "5-minute SDK onboarding for internal teams"
Steps: copy environment variable, run hello script, open Console -> traces, bump canary flag.

9) Open questions / TODOs
- Do we want an official sandbox key rotation cadence? (security asks quarterly)
- Should SDK auto-attach a lightweight health-check endpoint for long-running services? (opinion: yes, opt-in)
- Add a short video (2-3 min) showing streaming behavior in terminal vs Console — Miguel to prototype.
- Decide canonical metric names with SRE (Rhea to own alignment).

10) Links + references
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEVEXP/SDK-Home
- Regression ticket template: JIRA-DEVEXP-789
- SDK repo PR (example): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/214

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc as a single page hedge: one-pager + 2 example scripts + tiny-evals.
- Avoid duplicating long SDK API docs — link out. This is about speed and triage.
- When drafting final, extract '3-line troubleshooting' card for Support portal.

Authored: Emily Chen (draft). Miguel will mock the demo video; Rhea will confirm metric names.
